gen_risks.description: Ongoing armed conflict, civil unrest, and security instability in fragile areas (such as CAR, Chad, and Cameroon's North-West/South-West) could disrupt project execution, restrict physical access, and compromise health service delivery.
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and implement Security Risk Assessments (SRAs) and Security Management Plans (SMPs), adopt flexible implementation approaches in FCV zones, and engage local community partners for decentralized delivery.
gen_risks.evidence: Fragility in AFW is exacerbated by conflict and violence... Political instability, particularly in the North-West and South-West regions, may disrupt service delivery

gen_risks.description: Macro-fiscal instability, high public debt burdens, and declining national revenues across participating countries could lead to domestic funding shortfalls and jeopardize the financial sustainability of health security systems.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide technical assistance to integrate health security into national Medium-Term Expenditure Frameworks, establish budget coding and tracking, and leverage domestic resource mobilization and public-private partnerships.
gen_risks.evidence: A challenging macro-fiscal outlook... declining oil revenues... RoC's high debt burden limits public investment in health

gen_risks.description: Weak procurement capacity, complex market conditions in fragile settings, and governance bottlenecks could cause significant procurement delays, cost overruns, and supply chain disruptions for critical medical and laboratory commodities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Recruit experienced procurement specialists, deploy mandatory rated criteria for bidding, conduct early market engagements, strengthen contract management systems, and utilize STEP for real-time tracking.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement Risks include delays, governance issues, weak contract management, and limited market competition in fragile settings.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate financial management capacity, decentralized project activities in hard-to-reach areas, and multi-agency execution increase the risk of financial control failures, delayed reporting, and ineligible or questionable expenditures.
gen_risks.mitigation: Customize project accounting software, update financial management manuals, perform quarterly risk-based internal audits, retain qualified financial staff, and submit annual audited project financial statements.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall FM residual risk rating is assessed as Substantial... activities under the project like workshops, trainings... generate questionable expenditures in Cameroon

gen_risks.description: Increasing climate vulnerability and extreme weather events, such as severe flooding and droughts, risk damaging healthcare infrastructure and escalating vector-borne and waterborne disease outbreaks across the sub-region.
gen_risks.mitigation: Enforce EDGE level 1 energy-efficiency and climate-resilience standards for facility refurbishments, integrate climate hazard data into early warning surveillance systems, and update health sector contingency plans.
gen_risks.evidence: Climate change is a primary driver of health emergencies in Central Africa... More frequent flooding events in CAR and Chad drive recurrent cholera outbreaks

gen_risks.description: Improper management, handling, and disposal of hazardous biological, chemical, and infectious healthcare and laboratory waste generated during disease testing could result in environmental contamination and public health risks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Update and implement national Healthcare and Biomedical Waste Management Plans, enforce strict biosafety protocols in project laboratories, and train staff on safe hazardous waste disposal.
gen_risks.evidence: laboratories will be supplied with reagents, chemicals, and equipment that may constitute medical waste once used.

gen_risks.description: The expansion of frontline health workforces and civil works labor influx in local communities creates substantial risks of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse and Sexual Harassment (SEA/SH).
gen_risks.mitigation: Develop and enforce country-specific SEA/SH Action Plans, hire dedicated gender/GBV specialists in PIUs, establish GBV-sensitive grievance redress mechanisms, and mandate worker codes of conduct.
gen_risks.evidence: The overall project SEA/SH risks are judged to be substantial... increased presence of new health workforce... may create concerns of Sexual exploitation and abuse

gen_risks.description: Inadequate community engagement and consultation risks excluding vulnerable and marginalized populations—such as IDPs, refugees, rural women, and underserved groups—from project benefits and emergency health communications.
gen_risks.mitigation: Prepare, consult upon, and implement country-specific Stakeholder Engagement Plans (SEPs), deploy accessible Grievance Redress Mechanisms (GRMs), and conduct inclusive Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE) outreach.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks are substantial and relate to: (i) inadequate stakeholder engagement... (ii) the exclusion of vulnerable or disadvantaged groups

gen_risks.description: The digitization of disease surveillance and cross-border health data sharing without adequate privacy safeguards could expose sensitive personal health data to security breaches and non-compliance with data protection laws.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish standardized ethical data security and privacy protocols, ensure alignment with national data protection legislation, and integrate secure access controls into digital health platforms.
gen_risks.evidence: inadequate attention to ensure that guidelines established under the Program include considerations for and ethical data security protocols

gen_risks.description: Weak inter-ministerial coordination and fragmented institutional structures across human, animal, and environmental sectors could impede the effective operationalization of the One Health approach.
gen_risks.mitigation: Operationalize multisectoral National Steering Committees and technical committees, establish formal One Health coordination platforms, and execute formal inter-agency MoUs.
gen_risks.evidence: gaps are primarily due to limited domestic and regional resources, weak institutional capacities and governance mechanisms, and insufficient multisectoral coordination.

gen_risks.description: Severe shortages of specialized technical personnel and gender disparities in epidemiological and veterinary roles could limit national and subnational capacity to detect and manage public health threats.
gen_risks.mitigation: Expand Field Epidemiology Training Programs (FETP) and veterinary epidemiology (ISAVET) courses while implementing targeted outreach and gender targets to train and deploy female health workers.
gen_risks.evidence: women remain underrepresented in formal epidemiological training and decision-making... gaps in laboratory diagnostic capabilities... and the health workforce's ability

gen_risks.description: Bureaucratic and political bottlenecks in negotiating and adopting regional frameworks, sample transfer protocols, and data-sharing agreements across CEMAC member states could delay sub-regional health emergency responses.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize CEMAC's institutional mandate and the Regional Coordination Committee (RCC) to harmonize policies, standardize regional biosafety regulations, and expedite cross-border operational agreements.
gen_risks.evidence: Political and administrative inefficiencies could slow project execution.

gen_risks.description: Land acquisition, civil works, or construction/rehabilitation of health facilities and laboratories could cause temporary economic displacement or minor land use restrictions for local communities.
gen_risks.mitigation: Conduct thorough environmental and social screening of all sub-projects, prepare site-specific Resettlement Plans where necessary, and prioritize existing government land to prevent physical displacement.
gen_risks.evidence: Potential social risks... land acquisition impacts associated with new constructions... Resettlement Plans and Indigenous Peoples plan as needed

gen_risks.description: Inadequate laboratory equipment maintenance, supply chain delays for diagnostic reagents, and weak quality management systems could lead to diagnostic inaccuracies or failure during major disease outbreaks.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish interconnected national/regional laboratory networks, support WHO SLIPTA quality accreditation, enforce biosafety/biosecurity guidelines, and finance equipment maintenance contracts.
gen_risks.evidence: region commonly faces significant gaps in laboratory diagnostic capabilities... quality control, biosafety & biosecurity

gt_risks.description: Political and governance risk (Moderate), considering fragility, socio-political instability, violence and weak governance of beneficiary countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close engagement by the World Bank to coordinate activities with other key partners.

gt_risks.description: Technical design risk (Substantial), considering the complexities of coordinating national-level and regional-level activities to align and build on each other, and the different levels of readiness at country-level.
gt_risks.mitigation: Exploring the possibility of a coordinated implementation arrangement with CEMAC as the lead technical coordination body for regional activities.

gt_risks.description: Weak institutional capacity for implementation and sustainability (Substantial), combined with overstretched or nonexistent PIUs in respective countries.
gt_risks.mitigation: Strengthening the existing PIUs and intensive capacity building and targeted TA for newly established PIUs.

gt_risks.description: Fiduciary risk (Substantial) due to weak governance structures and inadequate FM systems.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on fiduciary processes.

gt_risks.description: E&S risk (Substantial) given the security risks associated with service delivery in FCV (fragility, conflict, and violence) settings.
gt_risks.mitigation: Close implementation support by the World Bank, including TA as well as additional training and coaching on managing E&S risks.
